title: Dark Matter, Black Holes and Gravitational Waves
notes: **Dark matter:** matter that does not emit, absorb or reflect light, but whose presence is inferred from gravitational effects on visible matter. It makes up about 85% of the total matter in the universe.

**Evidence for dark matter:** galaxy rotation curves remain flat at large radii, implying more mass than can be seen. Galaxy clusters show gravitational lensing stronger than visible matter can produce.
**Black hole:** a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape. The boundary is the event horizon.
**Event horizon radius (Schwarzschild):** $R_s = 2GM/c^2$. For a solar-mass black hole, $R_s \approx 3\,\text{km}$.

**Gravitational waves:** ripples in spacetime caused by accelerating masses, predicted by Einstein in 1916 and first detected in 2015 by LIGO from merging black holes. They travel at the speed of light and carry energy away from the source.
